title: Forcepoint Neo to Netskope Migration (Legacy Web Filtering)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (migration off a legacy web-filtering agent to Netskope; policy translation, coexistence, agent cutover, live-traffic risk).
Netskope console internals are deferred to Netskope's official documentation (no fabricated menus); authored at the correct architectural/procedural level.
hook: Migrate off legacy web filtering to Netskope — without a gap in protection
problem: Replacing a legacy web-filtering platform like Forcepoint Neo is risky: leave both agents on and they fight over traffic; cut over too fast and you lose protection or break access. This solution gives you a controlled migration from Forcepoint Neo to Netskope — translate existing filtering policy, manage agent coexistence, steer traffic in stages, and decommission the legacy platform once Netskope is proven.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the migration model, mapping legacy web-filtering policy to Netskope, agent coexistence and steering conflicts, and the staged cutover and decommission.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Netskope tenant + SWG, the existing Forcepoint Neo configuration/policy export, Intune for agent management, a pilot group, change control) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: inventory and translate legacy policy, stand up Netskope policy, manage coexistence and remove the legacy agent in stages, validate parity, decommission Forcepoint, then expand.

5 PowerShell scripts — legacy-agent and policy discovery, post-migration parity validation, a migration coverage and conflict report, safe remediation (remove legacy agent), and a migration-ring group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: A controlled migration from Forcepoint Neo to Netskope — translate filtering policy, manage agent coexistence, steer traffic in stages, and decommission the legacy platform once Netskope is proven. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
